newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-HAGI TAKES FIFA AND UEFA TO COURT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAGI TAKES FIFA AND UEFA TO COURT.

text.p: Jean-Louis Dupont, the lawyer who changed the course of sporting history in the Bosman case, is looking to repeat the performance with a claim against FIFA, UEFA and Barcelona on behalf of Romanian midfielder Gheorghe Hagi.
The action is designed to allow players from countries with special treaties with the European Union to be treated on a par with EU players.
Xavier Anoveros, a lawyer who is working alongside Dupont, outlined his client's case on Friday.

"After the Bosman sentence no fee can be charged for a transfer if a player is out of contract...and players from countries which have labour equality agreements with the EU can have the same treatment as if they were community players," said Anoveros.

Barcelona had asked Galatarasay for 241 million pesetas ($1.84 million) as a fee for Hagi's transfer in the summer and have retained part of his final pay-cheque after both the club and Hagi refused to make the payment.

The case involving Belgian player Jean-Marc Bosman led to a rewriting of the rule-book a year ago concerning players' rights after a Brussels court outlawed quotas that limited the number of EU players in sports sides within the Union. It also changed the laws on players' transfers.
Bosmans's lawyer, Dupont, argues further that Barcelona, the European soccer body UEFA and the world body FIFA should not be allowed to endanger Hagi's professional relationship with Galatarasary.
Hagi also points to the fact that he had signed for Real Madrid in 1990 and had played in EU countries for six years before moving to Turkey.

Experts consulted by the Barcelona-based daily Sport prior to Friday's press conference said that Hagi could only have taken advantage of the EU legislation if he had signed for a club within the Union.
